## CP Pilot Course

- CP4285 is part of the **CP428x Emerging Topics in Computer Science** series at NUS Computing
- These are **pilot courses**, each run for a single semester, with the intention of eventually becoming a permanent offering
- Students should expect the course is **not yet fully mature** — content, assessments, and delivery are actively evolving
- The series exists to expose undergraduates to **emerging areas** before they become established curriculum

## Ethics Thread

- Ethical issues are **not an afterthought** — they are woven throughout every week
- Core themes: **bias, fairness, privacy, exposure, transparency, stakeholder impact**
- Recommendation systems shape everyday decisions: what people read, watch, buy, apply for

::: {.callout-warning}
These systems encode values and trade-offs. Understanding how they work means understanding what they optimise for — and at whose expense.
:::

## Essays

- **Two individual take-home essays**, each worth **10%**
- Short written analyses of recommender-system methods, evaluation choices, and social implications
- Approximately **2–3 week** turnaround; AI tools permitted but an AI declaration is **mandatory**

::: {.callout-note}
Essays assess your own critical thinking. AI may assist but must not substitute your analysis.
:::

# 04 Types of Recommendation Systems {background-color="#EF7C00"}

<!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     SLIDE TYPE 7 — Two-Column Layout
     ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

## A Card-Suit Framework for User Types

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
♠ **Spades — The Explorer**
- Seeks novelty and diversity
- Values serendipitous discovery

♥ **Hearts — The Social Connector**
- Influenced by friends and community
- Trusts collaborative signals
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
♦ **Diamonds — The Pragmatist**
- Goal-oriented, task-driven
- Values precision over diversity

♣ **Clubs — The Loyalist**
- Sticks to known preferences
- Values consistency and familiarity
:::
:::
